name: James Comer
role: US representative for Kentucky (2016–present); Kentucky agriculture commissioner (2012–2016)
summary: Comer supports business tax relief, deregulation, gun rights and restrictive abortion policy. His record also includes hemp legalization, targeted pharmacy regulation, welfare work requirements and qualified support for tariffs.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He rejected Medicare for All and public options as steps toward government-controlled healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In 2019 he opposed a $15 minimum and said market competition should determine wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He prefers market wage setting and business decisions over government mandates.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He generally calls for fewer business regulations, while supporting targeted controls on pharmacy benefit managers.

cut-welfare.rationale: He argues welfare reform should move able-bodied recipients off assistance into employment; this supports conditional retrenchment.

limit-guns.rationale: He opposes federal restrictions on lawful gun owners, including tighter private-transfer rules.

empower-police-military.rationale: He supports maintaining police budgets and equipment and rebuilding the military.

rehabilitation.rationale: He promotes prison vocational training to reduce repeat incarceration and support reintegration.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He opposed same-sex marriage and voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.

abortion-legal.rationale: He supports abortion restrictions and welcomed Dobbs returning abortion lawmaking to the states.

free-trade.rationale: He values agricultural export trade but supports tariffs for manufacturing and national security; his position is qualified.

nation-first.rationale: He explicitly prioritizes American interests and argues Ukraine aid funds could be better spent at home.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He supported the 2017 Syrian strike against chemical-weapons capabilities and proposed protecting refugees in a safe zone.

open-borders.rationale: He supports a southern border wall and opposes sanctuary cities.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2025 he said climate initiatives had gone too far and hindered domestic energy production.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He supports advanced nuclear development and new nuclear-fuel facilities around Paducah.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 he backed tariffs to counter unfair trade and protect strategic manufacturing, while acknowledging costs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He backs federal grants and resources for strategic nuclear reindustrialization, alongside private investment.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He calls for spending restraint and a balanced-budget amendment because of federal debt.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He promoted increased SNAP work requirements with training and transportation support.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He portrays senior officials as engaged in corrupt influence-peddling; this records his allegations, not findings of guilt.

separated-powers.rationale: He says Congress must restrain executive power and defends the constitutional judicial process.

party-controls-media.rationale: His bill would prohibit federal officials pressuring platforms to suppress lawful political speech.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He invokes constitutional speech and gun rights as constraints on federal officials.

non-intervention.rationale: He endorsed a limited US strike inside Syria, while opposing ground deployment and regime-change efforts.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He voted against adding federal civil-rights protections based on gender identity in the Equality Act.

term-limits.rationale: He signed a pledge for constitutional limits of three House terms and two Senate terms.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: His support for striking Syrian chemical-weapons facilities extends beyond defending the United States against attack.

future-generations.rationale: No recorded position on a public duty to future generations; passing on his own farmland is something nearby.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He supports a constitutional balanced-budget requirement.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He called broad federal student-loan forgiveness an unjust transfer to highly educated graduates.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: He made a statewide right-to-work law his first proposed gubernatorial priority.

voter-id.rationale: He urges passage of the SAVE Act and explicitly demands identification to vote.

notes: Reviewed the full 490-statement list and remaining nulls across all themes. Trade answers reflect the more recent 2025 qualified tariff support, rather than only his 2017 cautions. Hemp legalization does not establish support for legalizing recreational drugs generally. Opposition to unauthorized immigration does not alone establish a desired reduction in all immigration. AI adoption and oversight statements do not establish a wish to transfer political decision-making to algorithms. The 2026 sexual-abuse NDA proposal does not directly answer the broader harassment/arbitration item. January 6 pardon support was checked but does not establish that he endorses political violence. Allegations involving himself or the Biden family are not treated as judicial findings. No positions are inferred from party, religion or office.
